observations.description: Powering up and configuring data path of 400G-ZR and 400G-ZR-M optics is not instant and takes more time comparatively with other optics. So, user has to wait enough time before switching to new speed configuration. If user switches from one speed to other speed without waiting leads to interface down.
For ACX7100-32C and ACX7100-48C platforms, increase the Performance Monitoring (PM) Engine polling interval from one every 2 and 4 seconds, respectively, to 1 per second for both platforms.

Multiple evo-pfemand restarts in quick succession is not recommended. Quick succession (back-to-back CLI command execution) results in undefined behaviour. With in five minutes, beyond three restarts are not allowed..

G.8275.1- G.8273.2 1PPS cTE performance test might be marginally outside class-C for PTP BC on ACX7100-48L, especially for mixed speed port testing with combinations of 10G / 25G channelized ports and 100G ports. On each reboot, the 1PPS cTE measurement might be within the class-C measurement threshold, or might randomly be out of threshold by a few nanoseconds.

In a ACX7509 system with dual Routing Engines and FEB, when there is a power fault of primary FEB, a switchover should happen and backup Routing Engine and FEB will take up primary role. Post switchover a VMCore might be generated in the new Backup Routing Engine. This failure should not impact the system uptime. Post Vmcore backup Routing Engine reboots and comes back online.
ACX7100-48L:Interface takes more time or does not come up after picd restart.

HQoS - VoQ Statistics issue during scaled configuration with congestion. In scaled HQOS configuration with congestion across all queues due to unavailability of the system level packet buffers, packets are dropped irrespective of the queue priorities. These dropped packets are not be accounted as part of queue statistics.
Channels of 4x100g channelization flap after they are brought up.
DTE mask fails for cascaded setup with long run.

In Layer 3 interface (inet/inet6/mpls), if user configures IEEE802.1p classifier alone, then all the flow (inet/inet6/mpls) is classified. If additional non IEEE802.1p classifier (DSCP/EXP etc.,) is mapped to the same interface, then the unmapped family is not classified and is handled as best effort mode.
observations.workaround: User has to configure classifiers for all the families to do proper classification. In Layer 2 interface (ethernet-switching), if user configures IEEE802.1p classifier alone, then all the flow (l2/v4/v6/exp) is classified. If additional non IEEE802.1p classifier (DSCP/EXP etc.,) is mapped to the same interface, then the unmapped family is not classified and is handled as best effort mode. Workaround: User has to configure classifiers for all the families to do proper classification.

observations.description: In ACX7509, when the FEB is ungracefully jacked out first and subsequently plugged in, the newly inserted FEB does not come online after online command is issued for the newly inserted FEB. The FEB stays stuck in onlining state.

In the scaled setup with SRv6 micro sid for L3VPN VRFs (~2K) are enabled in single commit, few initial VRF might experience traffic outage.
observations.workaround: Deactivating and re-activating only the failed VRFs resolves the problem.

If you have multiple except configuration, one of the rules will definitely hit. A firewall rule specifies criteria for a packet and a target. If the packet does not match, the next rule in the chain is the examined. If the packet does match, then the next rule is specified by the value of the target, which can be the name of a user-defined chain or one of the special values ACCEPT, DROP, QUEUE, or RETURN.

When per queue level dedicated buffer calculated based on scheduler buffer-size configuration, any fractional dedicated buffer value rounded-off to closest lower full integer and programmed in hardware to avoid over allocation. Any unused port dedicated buffers after allocating dedicated buffers to all configured queues is allocated to first configured queue.

When class-of-service configurations are bound with interface through wildcard style and direct apply style together, direct apply style always take precedence. So when a direct bind of any class-of-service feature present on an interface, other class-of-service features (like scheduler, congestion notification profile, dedicated buffer profile, etc) applied using wildcard is ignored for that interface.
